"Create a cinematic 2D pixel art endless runner game inspired by Cookie Run.

Visual Style: Beautiful high-quality pixel art, smooth animations, cinematic lighting, glowing particle effects, dynamic parallax backgrounds, and atmospheric environments.

Gameplay:

- Automatic endless running.
- Jump and double jump.
- Slide under obstacles.
- Dash and special character skills.
- Collect coins, gems, and power-ups.
- Random obstacles and increasing difficulty.
- Boss chase events and combo scoring.

Characters:
Create 6 unique unlockable characters, each with different designs, animations, stats, passive abilities, and powerful active skills:

- Fire Warrior: Flame Dash.
- Moon Mage: Teleport.
- Wind Runner: Tornado.
- Shadow Assassin: Invisibility.
- Light Guardian: Divine Shield.
- Thunder Warrior: Lightning Strike.

Worlds: Enchanted Forest, Cyberpunk City, Volcanic Land, Frozen Kingdom, and Celestial Ruins. Each world has unique pixel art backgrounds and obstacles.

Features: Character selection, skill upgrades, character skins, missions, achievements, high scores, coins, gems, and progression system.

UI: Beautiful animated main menu, character selection, gameplay HUD, pause menu, and cinematic game over screen.

Important: Make the game fully playable with responsive jump and slide controls, functional character skills, smooth animations, satisfying effects, and optimized mobile touch controls.

Make it look and feel like a professional indie pixel art game, not a basic prototype.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a polished, playable cinematic pixel-art endless runner inspired by Cookie Run.

## Requirements
- Automatic running with jump/double-jump, slide, dash/character skills, collectibles, random obstacles, rising difficulty, boss chases, and combo scoring.
- Six distinct unlockable characters with unique skills and five themed worlds.
- Character selection, upgrades, skins, missions, achievements, high scores, progression, responsive UI, and mobile touch controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a standalone browser game in `index.html`, with canvas-rendered scenery and runner, inline CSS/JavaScript, and localStorage persistence.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a single-page game with an animated menu, runner selection/unlocks, skill-upgrade and mission/trophy panels, HUD, pause/game-over flows, collectibles, obstacles, combo scoring, and save data.
- Added five themed world palettes/backgrounds, six character identities/skills, keyboard and touch controls, and responsive layout.
- Initial JavaScript syntax check passed before the HTML document wrapper was added.

### Active
- Validate the current `index.html` after the latest document-wrapper edit; verify gameplay and capture/read a fresh screenshot.

### Blocked
- Playwright CLI could not launch because its expected Chromium executable was missing (`Browser "chromium" is not installed`); a custom config attempt also failed due config path handling. System Chromium is available.

## Next Move
1. Run a JavaScript syntax check and inspect the rendered page using system Chromium against the current `index.html`.
2. Exercise menu, character selection, play, jump/slide/skill, pause, and game-over flows; fix any issues found.
3. Save and inspect a fresh JPEG screenshot (max 1280px wide).

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Entire game implementation; currently the only source file changed for the build.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A Python HTTP server was started on port `3002`.
- The earlier screenshot `/tmp/opencode/spritebound.jpg` was captured before the final HTML wrapper was added and should not be treated as a current visual check.
- The user requested reasonable assumptions and a concise note of them on completion.
